clue.text: Preferring a direct approach, but not right onwards

indicators.note: but not tells us to drop the following word from the longer one

parts.note: forthright describes someone blunt and straight to the point
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about someone who likes being direct, yet not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes RIGHT from FORTHRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go forward from a point is to go onwards.

clue.text: Item for office copier cutting power by constant margin

indicators.note: the copier cuts into the line of letters, splitting it apart

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
C is a standard symbol for a constant
a lip is an edge or margin
an aper is one who apes, a copier

explanation.surface: Something in the office involving a photocopier and an electrical supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copier' looks like the office machine but means an imitator, one who apes; 'by' just sets the margin beside the constant.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire clip for holding sheets together is a standard piece of office stationery.

clue.text: Not out to spoil new recruit

parts.note: in cricket scores, n.o. stands for not out
to vitiate is to spoil or impair

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to ruin a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who is NOT OUT has 'n.o.' beside the score.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a novice entering a religious order or any group is a beginner or recruit.

clue.text: Prohibition also covers one naval seaman

indicators.note: covers means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: too means also
AB, an able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A ban that applies to a sailor too.
explanation.walkthrough: An able seaman is rated AB in the Royal Navy, one of the commonest crossword abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a forbidden subject or act is under a prohibition.

clue.text: Yacht breaking up on cape is likely to be long-remembered

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B places A after B

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape

indicators.note: a boat breaking up has its parts scattered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A yacht wrecked on a headland makes a memorable story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' rearranges YACHT; in an across clue 'on' puts it after the cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy tune or phrase sticks in the mind, so it is easily remembered.

clue.text: Carbon detected in chosen test for breastplate

indicators.note: something detected in a thing is found inside it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a pet is a chosen favourite
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A lab test reveals carbon in an item of armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detected in' puts C inside PET.
explanation.definitionFit: A pectoral is an ornament or armour plate worn on the chest, as a breastplate is.

clue.text: Offender's difficult sentence perhaps left for judge

indicators.note: left for judge means L takes the place of the judge's letter

parts.note: a jawbreaker is a word or phrase that is hard to say

explanation.surface: A criminal faces a harsh sentence, with the matter left to the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' looks like a prison term but is a string of words; a hard-to-pronounce one is a JAWBREAKER. 'left for' swaps its J for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who commits a crime has broken the law and is an offender.

clue.text: What might be confused with dug-up memory

indicators.note: words that sound nearly alike are easily confused when heard

parts.note: dug-up describes something mined from the ground

explanation.surface: A recollection that could be mistaken for something excavated.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay depends on MINED and the answer sounding almost the same when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The mind holds recollections, as in 'it came to mind', so it stands for memory.

clue.text: Rushed, needing time to go on and on

parts.note: ran means rushed

explanation.surface: Someone in a hurry who needs time to keep talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant is to speak at length in a loud, angry or tedious way.

clue.text: Cutting manner gets meat joints in pieces

indicators.note: in places the joints inside the pieces

parts.note: bits are pieces
a chine is a joint of meat cut along the backbone

explanation.surface: A butcher's way of cutting meat joints into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting manner' reads like butchery, but it means a spiteful way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting remarks are spiteful, and spitefulness of manner is called bitchiness.

clue.text: Extravagant faults we corrected

indicators.note: faults that are corrected are put right, rearranged here

explanation.surface: Someone admits to spending too much and fixing their failings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' rearranges the letters of FAULTS WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an extravagant person spends lavishly and squanders resources.

clue.text: The ending of restrictions affected island lobsters

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected

explanation.surface: Lifting fishing restrictions changes things for an island's lobster catch.
explanation.walkthrough: SCAMPI are Norway lobsters, also called langoustines.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are Norway lobsters, small crustaceans sold breaded in Britain.

clue.text: County head for Glamorgan was abolished

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: something abolished has gone, so went fits

explanation.surface: Glamorgan's council leader is gone along with the county.
explanation.walkthrough: Gwent and Glamorgan were Welsh counties; Gwent was itself abolished in 1996, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwent was a county in south-east Wales from 1974 to 1996.

clue.text: Run up debts recorded as without interest

parts.note: to incur debts is to run them up
IOUs are debts recorded in writing

explanation.surface: Someone builds up debts that are noted down as interest-free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' looks financial but means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an incurious person lacks curiosity, having no interest in things.

clue.text: Dripping replaced a trad suet

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A traditional suet swapped for beef fat in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dripping' looks like the cooking fat, fitting the suet, but means soaked. 'replaced' rearranges A TRAD SUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something soaking wet and dripping is saturated.

clue.text: Cromwell finally beheaded king, perhaps still faithful

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word
beheaded removes the first letter

parts.note: a king is an example of a royal

explanation.surface: Cromwell had the king beheaded, yet some stayed faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' takes R off ROYAL. Cromwell's Parliament beheaded Charles I, so the surface rings true; 'still' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone loyal stays true and faithful to a cause.

clue.text: Railway saved money mostly filling broken rail with copper

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped, and filling leads the shortened word into the front of what follows

parts.note: a fund is money saved up

indicators.note: a broken rail has its parts rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Money set aside to mend a broken rail with copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts FUND to FUN; 'broken' rearranges RAIL with CU into ICULAR. 'filling' only links the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A funicular is a cable railway up a steep slope.

clue.text: Fix part of drivetrain

indicators.note: part of signals the answer sits inside the word

explanation.surface: Repair a component of a car's drivetrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rivet is to fasten firmly, and to fix is to fasten.

clue.text: Where eggs are used, cover fruit so as to avoid runs

parts.note: a hat is a cover for the head

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out

parts.note: a cherry is a fruit
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: eggs, a cover and fruit, without letting it run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' suggests cooking, but the eggs are hatched. 'so as to avoid' drops one R from CHERRY. R is runs on a cricket scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchery is a place where eggs are hatched, so where eggs are put to use.

clue.text: Scale drawing of flat lacking a key

indicators.note: lacking means one letter is missing

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface
E is one of the musical keys A to G

explanation.surface: An architect's drawing of an apartment without a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means level. 'lacking' takes E from PLANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a drawing to scale of a building or area seen from above.

clue.text: Bag for cup of tea?

definitions.meaning: informal: something is your bag when it is what you like
your cup of tea is something you like, as in 'not my cup of tea'

explanation.walkthrough: Both look like tea-making, a teabag for a cup, but each is slang for what one likes best.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for what one favours, which is a liking or choice.

clue.text: Something tasteless with eggs about to turn

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
tat is cheap, tasteless stuff

explanation.surface: A bland egg dish is about to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' sounds like food going off in the egg picture, but it means to spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rotate is to turn about an axis.

clue.text: Sensualist score cut by French composer

indicators.note: cut by means the second piece goes into the first

parts.note: to score is to mark a line, so a score is a line
Jacques Ibert was a French composer

explanation.surface: Twenty pieces of music trimmed by a French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like twenty or music but means a line scratched into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a libertine leads a life of sensual pleasure.

clue.text: Cruise ship's bow line

parts.note: the prow is the front or bow of a ship

explanation.surface: A cruise ship's bow and line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruise' looks like a sea voyage but is a verb: to roam looking for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to prowl or cruise is to roam about looking for prey or company.

clue.text: One with plenty of work on hand

definitions.text: One with plenty of work on hand

parts.words: One with plenty of work on hand
parts.note: reads as someone busy, but literally a worker whose job is done on people's hands and nails

explanation.definitionFit: A manicurist trims and polishes fingernails, so the work is literally on a hand.

clue.text: Cried after twists and turns exposed

indicators.note: after places the word before it behind the word that follows

parts.note: a road winds when it twists and turns
wept means cried

explanation.surface: Someone wept after a winding journey in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a windswept place is exposed to the wind.

clue.text: Gloomy about social security after one gets the sack

indicators.note: about puts the first word around what follows

parts.note: dismal means gloomy

indicators.note: after puts social security behind one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sinks into gloom on benefits after losing their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the sack is an idiom for being fired from a job.

clue.text: Sicken oddly inside like many diseases of the intestines

indicators.note: inside places the picked letters within the other word

parts.note: many diseases are viral

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A stomach illness that makes one feel strangely sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd-numbered letters S, C, E of 'Sicken'.
explanation.definitionFit: Visceral relates to the viscera, the internal organs such as the intestines.

clue.text: Fool to shout abuse crossing street

indicators.note: crossing means the word goes across and around the other

parts.note: to jeer is to shout abuse

explanation.surface: An idiot yells insults while crossing the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A court jester was a professional fool who entertained a ruler.

clue.text: Initially working a long time for pay

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Working a long time for one's wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wages are the pay earned for work.

clue.text: Showing unpredictability, reversing an unknown fate

indicators.note: reversing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: doom means fate
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone's fortunes turn on an uncertain fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns DOOM into MOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A moody person's temper changes unpredictably.

clue.text: Murdered and cut up with head missing

indicators.note: with head missing means the first letter goes

parts.note: diced means cut into small cubes

explanation.surface: A victim killed and chopped up, the head never found.
explanation.walkthrough: ICED is slang for killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: to ice someone is to murder them.
